result.message: Reviewed the selu_ candidate (.best_kernel.py == the round-3 solution sha256 0e782a69… in .ledger.json and optimize_definition_output.json) against the supplied catalog (definition/oracle/correctness/timing) and the measurement receipts. The math (scale=1.0507009873554805, alpha=1.6732632423543772, fp32 intermediate for non-fp16, in-place write, returns A) matches torch.selu_ semantics; the oracle is independent of the candidate and there is no torch.ops/fallback computation, no host synchronisation in the hot path, and no test-specific shapes/values. The main risks are (a) the dispatch branches that dominate the measured geo_mean (unmasked tile kernel kind 0 and persistent grid-stride kernel kind 2) are never exercised by any correctness workload, whose shapes are all masked/early-return/strided, while timing workloads are never output-checked; (b) the pointer-keyed direct-launcher fast path ignores the device, grows without bound, and depends on an undocumented positional launcher ABI with inconsistent trailing argument counts and no launch-time fallback; (c) int32 index arithmetic caps the kernels below 2^31 elements and every non-fp16 dtype is forced through a float32 intermediate, which would silently degrade float64 input (uncovered by the catalog). Correctness within the covered paths (masked tail, strided, empty, n=1) is consistent: all 24 correctness workloads passed in the ledger with errors inside the catalog tolerances. Findings are advisory per the code-review policy.
